I’ve made ten jars like this, crimson pots, thrown crimson clay that’ll eventually be coated in a crimson glaze and then finally, they’ll be reduction fired, oh, there’s also some bronze in the mix, small fragments, which when put through the kiln turn into these red haloed flecks of metal. All of that might sound quite over the top but it’s a deep red with underlying tones of black and hopefully they resemble some of the tests I’ve fired in the past… fingers crossed. They require a different approach when crafting them, especially during the turning stage. As the particles of grog the body contains are constantly torn out I have to go back over the surface, burnishing it and smoothing it as I go to get rid of the overly prominent scratches these splinters of ceramic create. I lost a few pieces from attempting to fix oval openings, they were thrown round, but as clay slowly dries it’s quite common for it to subtlety warp. I tried to gentle press the opening back into a round shape and I felt something give; upon further inspection I found a hairline crack in the rim. Grogged clays might be tough during the throwing and the firing but it’s brittle stuff during the trimming stage, especially when trimmed as thinly as this. #clay #handmade #satisfying #pottery #ceramics

This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. So tell me, what makes you stay hopeful when life feels extra gloopy? #ceramicartist #dopaminedecor #glitterinlay #rainbowart #processvideo

pricing my work is truly my LEAST favourite thing 😭  especially after trying to look closer at the numbers behind my small ceramic business. i’m trying to map out the potential 1, 3, and 5 year revenue and expense projections to see if investing in a kiln and building this business actually makes any sense. at my current $30-$65 price point, i’m losing money selling my work and cannot justify a kiln. i’ve made the terrifying decision to raise my prices by 25-30%. the money will go towards expanding production (investing. in a kiln & shelving), upgrading my website, expanding to ship to the US, and finally, offering private lessons and workshops.  with the price increase, I will still need to survive 6 months - 1 year without a livable wage / making profit. i’ll be focusing on my higher-margin petal bowls and bring in some more affordable $25 products like spoon rests and trinket dishes to keep things as accessible as possible. my mugs are not viable as they take me 2hrs each, but i’m going to keep making them for now and hope i can speed it up. no more lidded jars outside of speciality collections as the margins are too low.  i’m also going to try to secure 1-2 freelance social media clients to provide me with some supplement income as a buffer. this is the behind the scenes of small ceramics business’ that you normally don’t see, because it’s not nearly as cute or fun as the pots themselves. #potterybusiness #ceramics #smallbusiness #priceincrease #handmadeceramics

I’m a sucker for the making of pots, the joyous throwing and trimming, but what comes after, the waxing, glazing and firing, is more of a laborious task that normally ends up being highly repetitive. I don’t mind the work, I keep my headphones on and listen to stories throughout the day, yet I definitely experience more pain in my hands from these processes, as compared to throwing and trimming. Specifically, it’s the grasping of pots as I fettle the surface clean, as the fingers that are gripped so tightly around the object cannot move, otherwise they rub down the surface and create thin patches that show in the finished pots. This means that the hand that holds the pots is tensed for hours on end with my fingers pressed against a relatively powdery surface, if I squeeze too hard, the clay can fracture and come off of the vessel and too loose a grip means my digits glide across the surface, again creating thin spots. It’s hard to describe, but essentially this hand becomes a vice whilst the other carefully cleans the surface. It’s a skill, just like any other in the making process. #pottery #glazing #glaze #howto #craftsmanship #ceramics

If you’d like to see a far more thorough exploration of these vases, I recommend watching the 40-minute version that’s on my YouTube channel, a link to which you can find via the Linktree in my profile’s biography.   This week I’m making some of my favourite pots, they aren’t really about function, at least that is not what I’m thinking about whilst I create them. These angular vases with a protruding line across one side are simple, decorative objects and a welcome change after a few weeks of focusing solely on functional ware. I take my time with them and pay close attention to proportion and surface and how the line travels and over the past few years they’ve changed quite a lot.   They used to appear squatter and the lines were heavier and less defined but after making many batches, they have gradually become taller and more refined, in my opinion. The carved line has followed that shift, it’s sharper now, more deliberate and despite only being a relatively small addition, the change it makes is drastic. Most of my work is thrown on the wheel and naturally symmetrical and therefore this detail interrupts that uniformity. It gives the vessel a direction and a front. It catches the light and throws a shadow across the flat planes and somehow that single line makes the pots feel more figurative, especially when they are grouped together.   If you happen to click over and watch the longer edition, thank you, it means so much!   #pottery #vase #sculpture #handmade #ceramics
